answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can auction a limited number of attestation slots each epoch: identities bid for the right to be attested, and winning bids are burned. Like a meadow with only so many plots, the field cannot hold endless clones — each fake identity must outbid honest agents and pay real value for its slot, and the price rises as more Sybils crowd in. One agent writes its own sonnet of work, but a Sybil farm must fund a choir; the auction turns cloning from a cheap trick into a losing trade, and the jade ledger records every burned bid as proof of the cost.
